sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers s. 31–36 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: s. 31–36 must be broken into definitions, operative words, conditions, exceptions, savings and consequences. Map the agreement and commercial records to each statutory ingredient.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:
1. Establish the transaction and parties.
2. Identify the statutory trigger in s. 31–36.
3. Prove each constituent fact.
4. Test exceptions and defences.
5. Identify the precise legal consequence.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 31–36 define contingent contracts and govern enforcement when the specified collateral event happens or does not happen, when a living person’s conduct makes the event impossible, when a fixed-time event occurs or fails, and when the contingency is impossible from the outset.

Definition: A contingent contract makes performance depend on an uncertain future collateral event and is enforceable only according to the statutory contingency rules.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the underlying contract.
2. Identify the collateral uncertain event.
3. Determine whether the contract depends on the event happening or not happening.
4. Apply the relevant fixed-time and impossibility rule.
5. Do not treat a wager as a contingent contract merely because both involve uncertainty.
examples: A promises to pay B a sum if B’s house is destroyed by fire; the obligation is contingent on the specified collateral event and becomes enforceable according to the statutory rule when that contingency occurs.
problemApplication: Apply sections 31–36 to a factual problem by identifying the statutory trigger, testing every ingredient, checking exceptions or limitations, and stating the legal consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 31–36 define contingent contracts and govern enforcement when the specified collateral event happens or does not happen, when a living person’s conduct makes the event impossible, when a fixed-time event occurs or fails, and when the contingency is impossible from the outset.
